topics.label: Introduction and Overview of Cancer Hallmarks
topics.groupedBecause: This topic introduces the lecture structure, learning outcomes, and the conceptual framework of the hallmarks of cancer.

topics.label: Growth Signal Autonomy and Proliferative Signaling Pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how mutations in signaling pathways such as Wnt, receptor tyrosine kinases, and TGF-beta enable cancer cells to sustain proliferation and achieve growth signal independence.

topics.label: Differentiation Block in Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the mechanism and consequences of impaired differentiation in tumors using hematopoietic malignancies and colorectal tissue architecture as examples.

topics.label: Resistance to Apoptosis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic focuses on how cancer cells evade programmed cell death through mutations disrupting the balance of p53, Bax, and BCL2.

topics.label: Replicative Immortality and Senescence Bypass
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how cancer cells overcome the Hayflick limit and normal p53-dependent senescence barriers through telomere maintenance and TERT upregulation.

topics.label: Reprogramming Cellular Metabolism
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the metabolic rewiring of cancer cells, including aerobic glycolysis, the Warburg effect, Krebs cycle mutations, and onco-metabolite production.

topics.label: Inducing Angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the biological necessity, developmental timing, regulatory balance, and therapeutic targeting of new blood vessel formation in tumors.

topics.label: Invasion and Metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores the multistep metastatic cascade, mechanisms of tumor dissemination, diagnostic tools, and genomic traits associated with secondary tumor colonization.

topics.label: Lecture Summary and Closing Remarks
topics.groupedBecause: This topic concludes the lecture with a synthesis of how cancer hallmarks integrate and brief closing administrative remarks.
